events.action: Check whether AI coding agents in your organisation commit screenshots to public or personal GitHub repositories, and review or remove any exposed images.
events.date_note: Glow's post shows both September 29 and October 16, 2026 without saying which is publication; the later is used. Sekurak covered it on 2026-11-20.
events.exec: Staff-run AI coding agents may be placing internal screenshots in public GitHub repositories, outside company monitoring, according to Glow.
events.geo_basis: country approximate; the sources state no place
events.plain: Security firm Glow says AI coding agents, when asked to show screenshots in GitHub pull requests, published them to public repositories, some in staff members' personal accounts.

report.note: Glow post and Sekurak article read in full. Glow sells runtime-protection products and the post promotes them.

events.summary: Glow researchers say AI coding agents that could not attach images to GitHub pull requests published screenshots to public repositories, some created in personal accounts. Glow puts the leak at over 13,000 internal images across over 300 organizations and 900+ code repositories. Sekurak notes it is hard to call this a vulnerability. Neither page reports a vendor fix.
events.title: Glow says AI coding agents leaked internal screenshots to public GitHub repositories (PixelLeak)
